Meeting header: 2025-11-20 16:00 PST — Duration: ~52 minutes. Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Sami Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Apogee Head of Data), Markus Berg (CTO), Priya Nair (ML Eng).

[00:00] Jordan: ok hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick check, audio okay?
[00:07] Lena: yep, good here.
[00:10] Jordan: great. Agenda — recap last week's guardrail changes, look at the new eval spreadsheet Sami pushed, and then decide next steps for regression runs and capacity testing.
[00:25] Sami: i'll share my screen in a sec, but quick note, the eval set now has per-prompt confidence and token-cost columns; some of the billing prompts spiked in hallucination false positives after we tightened the output constraints.
[00:40] Markus: when you say 'spiked' how big are we talking? percentage?
[00:45] Sami: roughly from 2.1% to 3.8% for that subgroup, so small but surpasses your threshold of 3%. it's concentrated on longer multi-turn billing scenarios where the model truncates context and starts guessing account ids.
[01:05] Priya: yeah we saw that in prod traces too, there's a handful of queries that were previously fine. could be tokenization differences after quantization.
[01:14] Jordan: ok so we have hypothesis A — prompt drift from a new prompt template; hypothesis B — quantization profile interplay; hypothesis C — caching/K-V cache mismatch on resumed sessions. 
[01:28] Lena: K-V cash? do you mean KV cache?
[01:31] Sami: yeah KV cache sorry, the auto-transcript will say K-V cash ha.
[01:35] Lena: lol noted.
[01:38] Jordan: Sami, walk us through the sheet.

[02:00] Sami: screen — first tab is the baseline 10k prompts, second tab is the focused billing subset. Column H is 'hallucination flag' — it's binary, but we also have a confidence float column. For example prompt ID B-432 shows hallucination true at conf 0.62 and token-cost 112. The prior run had conf 0.88 and hallucination false.
[02:35] Markus: is that the run with the new quantized weights?
[02:38] Sami: yes that's the quant profile B we rolled for cost-savings. It's the lighter 4-bit config.
[02:45] Markus: hmm — performance gains at cost of some accuracy, not unexpected. can we get a run with profile A (8-bit) to compare?
[02:51] Sami: absolutely, already queued. but note the difference seems prompt-specific; some prompts actually improved with B.
[03:05] Priya: that matches our intuition: mixed effects.

[03:20] Jordan: okay next section — guardrails. We added a hard stop on named entities and an output-filter so that any account-like pattern triggers clarification. The filters caught 12 instances in the last 48h, but two slipped through.
[03:38] Lena: what does 'slipped through' mean operationally? user-visible bad answers?
[03:42] Sami: in two cases the model paraphrased an account number in an indirect way and the regex didn't catch it. We can tighten the regex and add a sanity-check step — maybe a verify step that calls a lightweight reranker.
[03:58] Markus: reranker adds cost though. what's the delta?
[04:02] Sami: rough ballpark — +5–8% token cost per affected request depending on cache hit. For low frequency it's negligible but on heavy billing flows could add up.

[04:20] Lena: can we instead increase the guardrail threshold so it flags more aggressively but doesn't call the reranker unless confidence < 0.4?
[04:28] Jordan: yes that's the pattern we recommend — tiered fallback: filter -> clarification prompt -> reranker if still ambiguous. keeps cost bounded.

[04:38] Priya: question on observability — are the audit logs capturing the intermediate reranker outcomes and the exact prompt sent? compliance wants full request/response logs for 30 days.
[04:48] Sami: yes — Redwood Inferencing (sic) can surface request/response pairs in the audit log; there is a PII redaction toggle and KMS integration. For SOC2 we usually recommend storing only hashes plus encrypted payloads in S3 via your KMS.
[05:05] Markus: good. need that in writing for procurement.

[05:20] Jordan: i'll drop the SOC2/arch note with examples. back to regressions — Sami you mentioned you queued a quant-A run — timeline?
[05:33] Sami: should finish tonight, but we need to run the regression suite against the 3 new prompt sets Apogee shared last sprint — haven't got those yet.
[05:42] Priya: sorry about that, we'll upload by tomorrow EOD — 3 edge-case prompts and some anonymized customer examples.
[05:49] Lena: also, one more ask — can we get per-token latency percentiles? we care about p95 for the billing workflow.
[05:56] Sami: yes, p50/p95/p99 are in the telemetry tab; for the recent runs p95 jumped from 380ms to 470ms under B during cold starts. caching helps but cold KV misses are painful.

[06:15] Jordan: that suggests testing dedicated pool for steady qps. Markus, are you ok with a 2-week dedicated eval if the numbers look promising?
[06:24] Markus: yes, we budgeted for a short dedicated pilot. want to see the price delta though.

[06:35] Sami: aside from cost there's also deployment: private VPC option introduces network egress differences — we can show you estimated latency with region proximity.
[06:45] Priya: our compliance team will prefer VPC for sensitive traces.

[06:52] Jordan: noted. next, prompt auditing — Priya had flagged a handful of system prompts that were modified last sprint; can you explain the change?
[07:02] Priya: we shortened the system prompt to reduce token cost, removed some explicit denials, which might be lowering the behavior penalty for hallucinations.
[07:12] Jordan: ah — that explains decreased strictness. Recommendation: keep the explicit guardrail statements in system prompt and use output filters to shorten responses instead of removing safety clauses.
[07:23] Lena: do we have a diff view of system prompts across runs?
[07:27] Sami: yes — the sheet has a 'prompt diff' column but it's a bit unwieldy. I'll export a clean diff and attach.

[07:40] Jordan: ok let's enumerate concrete experiments: 1) quant-A vs quant-B regression on billing subset; 2) tighten regex + add clarification step for account-like entities; 3) run dedicated pool at target qps for load test; 4) re-add explicit lines to system prompt and measure hallucination delta. Any objections?
[07:58] Markus: sounds good.

[08:05] (noise)

[08:15] Priya: quick nit — when we re-run regression, can Sami include the seed and randomization params? we need reproducibility.
[08:22] Sami: yes, full run metadata will be attached.

[08:30] Jordan: procurement question — Lena, what's the internal timeline for decision on dedicated capacity?
[08:36] Lena: we want to decide by mid-december, but it depends on the regression results and the pricing delta.

[08:45] Jordan: okay. i'll get you a delta by Nov 26. Sami will run regressions and share the per-prompt CSV by Nov 24. Priya will send the edge-case prompts by Nov 25.

[09:00] Sami: one more technical point — we saw a couple false positives from the guardrail on non-billing docs where 12-digit numbers are actually invoice numbers that we should allow. We can add a whitelist and contextual checks.
[09:12] Priya: yes, invoice numbers are different format; we can provide a regex whitelist.

[09:20] Jordan: good. last section — risk summary for procurement: 1) small hallucination drift with quant-B; 2) minor latency volatility on cold starts; 3) guardrail misses that we can tighten. mitigation: reruns, dedicated pool short test, stricter filters + clarification. Any more?
[09:40] Markus: nothing else.

[09:45] Jordan: wrap up — recap and next steps.
[09:50] Lena: thanks everyone.

[09:55] End of meeting.
